stem: A survey manager divides the country into 8 geographic zones. She then randomly selects 3 of those zones and surveys every person living within the selected zones. Which sampling method does this describe?

per_option_rationale.rationale: The population is divided into geographic groups called clusters. Whole clusters are randomly selected and all members within those clusters are surveyed.
Stratified sampling selects a random sample from within each group, not all members from selected groups. The student confuses cluster with stratified.
The student focuses on 'every person within selected zones' and misidentifies the regular coverage as a systematic interval pattern.
The student fixates on 'randomly selects' and concludes simple random sampling, ignoring the group-selection structure that defines clustering.

explanation: In cluster sampling, the population is divided into groups called clusters. A random sample of clusters is chosen and every unit in the selected clusters is surveyed. Here the zones are clusters, so this is cluster sampling.

explanation_sections.punchline: Cluster sampling selects whole groups as the sampling unit, then surveys every member in the selected groups. That is exactly what happens here: 3 zones are picked, and every person in those zones is surveyed.
explanation_sections.approach: State the definition: cluster sampling = divide population into groups (clusters), randomly select some clusters, survey all members of each selected cluster. Contrast the confusable: stratified sampling also groups the population first but then draws a sample from within each group - not all members. Decision shortcut: ask whether the whole group is taken or a subset from each group.
explanation_sections.lesson: The only structural difference between cluster and stratified sampling is what happens after grouping. Cluster: select some groups, take all members of those groups. Stratified: keep all groups, take a sample from each.
explanation_sections.timing: 45 seconds. Two facts decide it: groups are formed, then entire groups are surveyed. Match to cluster definition and mark. 20 seconds is sufficient.
